lessons.unit: Spring 1: Special days, summer and numbers
lessons.title: Bridge: my name, and this and that
lessons.bigQuestion: How do I tell someone who I am in Arabic?
objectives: To understand how to introduce myself and point to things in Arabic
successCriteria: All: say اِسْمِي (ismi) and my name
Most: ask مَا اسْمُكَ؟ (ma smuka?) and answer
Some: use هٰذَا (hadha) for near and ذٰلِكَ (dhalika) for far
lessons.crossCurricular: English: a sentence needs a naming word, just like هٰذَا كِتَابٌ (This is a book)
lessons.smsc: Social: greeting others with salam and learning their names

keywords.def: what is your name? (to a boy)

hook.text: When you meet a new friend, what is the first thing you say? How could you say it in Arabic?
hook.a: As-salamu 'alaykum, then my name: اِسْمِي ... (ismi ...).

islamicLink.text: Allah says that He sent the Qur'an down in Arabic so that we may understand (Yusuf 12:2). Every Arabic word we learn helps us understand the Qur'an a little more.

starter.q: Bismillah. Which letter is this: ب? A) ba B) ta C) tha
How many dots does ت (ta) have?

teach.heading: Saying my name
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Say ismi and your name, then pupils say theirs one by one, cameras on. Point out that ismi is one word in Arabic.

teach.heading: Asking a name
bullets: مَا اسْمُكَ؟ (ma smuka?) to a boy
مَا اسْمُكِ؟ (ma smuki?) to a girl
teach.note: Model a short talk: salam, ma smuka?, ismi ... Show that the ending changes for a boy (-ka) and a girl (-ki). Pupils ask the pupil after them.

teach.heading: This and that
bullets: هٰذَا كِتَابٌ (hadha kitabun) = this is a book
ذٰلِكَ بَابٌ (dhalika babun) = that is a door
teach.note: Hold a book close to the camera: hadha. Point far to the door: dhalika. Pupils copy the action and say the word.

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: Give 30 seconds, then share the results.

check.q: The book is far away. Which word do we use?
check.why: ذٰلِكَ (dhalika) points to something far away; هٰذَا (hadha) is for near.

practice.model:
Start with اِسْمِي (ismi).
Add the name: يُوسُفُ.
Say it all: ismi Yusuf.

practice.q: A pen is near you. Say: This is a pen.

independent.q: Core: Write اِسْمِي (ismi) and your name in Arabic letters, three times neatly.
independent.model: Teacher writes اِسْمِي on the whiteboard, joining س and م, then writes their own name after it.

independent.q: Extend: Write هٰذَا كِتَابٌ and ذٰلِكَ بَابٌ and say what each means.
independent.a: This is a book. That is a door.

independent.q: Stretch: Write a short talk: salam, ask a name, give your name.

exit.q: What does اِسْمِي (ismi) mean? A) my name is B) this is C) that is
Big question: how do I tell someone who I am in Arabic?
exit.a: Say salam, then اِسْمِي (ismi) and my name.

lessons.homework: Introduce yourself in Arabic to someone at home: salam, ismi and your name.
lessons.send: SEND: name card with اِسْمِي already written, pupil adds their name. EAL: picture cards for book and door. Stretch: use مَا اسْمُكِ؟ (ma smuki?) for a girl.

Portal arabic y3 lesson 1 (this and that), reused for the bridge
Kitabi: introducing myself (CHECK IN KITABI)
Name card template (portal worksheet)
A book and mini-whiteboard and pen

lessons.unit: Unit 1: Near, far and describing
lessons.title: Describing things: big, small, new and old
objectives: Use four adjectives with masculine nouns
Put the adjective after the noun
Read and write short descriptions
starter: Say 'This is a mosque' in Arabic.
Say 'That is a house' in Arabic.
What is the difference between haadhaa and dhaalika?

teach.heading: Describing words
teach.note: Use hand gestures: wide arms for big, finger and thumb close for small. Pupils echo and add gestures. Ask: what is big in your house? what is small? Use objects they know.

teach.heading: New and old
teach.note: Hold up a new notebook and an old one. Use the sentence: haadhaa kitaab jadeed. Pupils say the sentence. Highlight that jadeed and qadeem end in ‘-eed’/’-eem’, a long 'ee' sound.

teach.heading: Adjective after the noun
teach.note: In English the adjective comes before the noun (big house). In Arabic it comes after (bayt kabeer). Common error: putting it first. Use two coloured cards and place them in the right order. Pupils rearrange the cards.

teach.heading: Making more sentences
teach.note: Pupils read each sentence, then translate. Pronounce carefully. Ask: how do you know these are masculine? (haadhaa/dhaalika and the nouns). Quick game: teacher says an English description, pupils find the Arabic.

teach.heading: Match and say
teach.note: Give a bank of pictures: big house, small car, new pen, old book. Pupils match and say sentences using haadhaa. Walk around breakout rooms and check word order.

practice: Show a picture of a big house; pupils say haadhaa bayt kabeer.
Match opposite words: kabeer/sagheer and jadeed/qadeem.
Describe three pictures using haadhaa + noun + adjective.
Pair task: one pupil draws, the partner says the sentence.
independent: Write four sentences about masculine things using the adjectives.
Draw a big mosque and a small house; label with Arabic sentences.
exit: Where does the adjective go: before or after the noun?
lessons.homework: Write two sentences about two objects at home: one new and one old (e.g. هَذَا كِتَابٌ قَدِيمٌ).
lessons.send: SEND: picture cards with Arabic labels and colour-coded endings. EAL: provide bilingual flashcards. Stretch: add two adjectives to one noun with wa, e.g. بَيْتٌ كَبِيرٌ وَجَدِيدٌ.

lessons.unit: Unit 2: Feminine words and 'my'
lessons.title: Describing girl words: big, small, beautiful
objectives: Make adjectives feminine by adding ة
Say sentences with feminine nouns and adjectives
Use jameela (beautiful) to describe things
starter: Say 'that is a new book' in Arabic.

teach.heading: Feminine nouns
teach.note: Show pictures. Recall that most feminine nouns end in ة. Pupils spot the round ending on the board. Ask them to find ة in each word.

teach.heading: Feminine adjectives
teach.note: Show the pattern: add ة to the adjective to describe a girl word. Use arrow animation. Misconception: pupils forget to change the adjective. Insist: girl word, girl adjective.

teach.heading: Beautiful
bullets: Allah is beautiful and loves beauty
teach.note: Teach jameel/jameela. Authentic hadith: 'Allah is beautiful and loves beauty' (Sahih Muslim). Link to noticing beauty in creation. Practise: hadeeqa jameela.

teach.heading: Making sentences
teach.note: Pupils read in chorus, then pairs. Translate the sentences. Pupils point to the ة endings on both words. Highlight the match: both words end with ة.

teach.heading: Boy or girl sentence?
teach.note: Compare boy and girl sentences side by side. Ask: what changes? (haadhihi, ة twice). Play a game: teacher says a noun, pupils say the full sentence with an adjective of their choice.

practice: Recall the six adjectives we have learned.
Say 'this is a big house' and 'that is a new pen' in Arabic.
Describe pictures with feminine nouns and adjectives.
Fix mistakes: هَذِهِ سَيَّارَةٌ كَبِيرٌ → correct it.
independent: Write three sentences with feminine nouns.
Draw a beautiful garden and write a sentence.
lessons.homework: Write four sentences describing things at home using haadhaa/haadhihi and an adjective.
lessons.send: SEND: use sentence frames with the two options highlighted. EAL: read sentences aloud in pairs with a buddy. Stretch: write a short description of your room using at least three adjectives.

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Special days, summer and numbers
lessons.title: Bridge: boy words, girl words and my
lessons.bigQuestion: How can I tell if an Arabic word is a girl word?
objectives: To understand that Arabic words are masculine or feminine and how to say 'my'
successCriteria: All: spot ة (ta marbutah) at the end of a feminine word
Most: choose هٰذَا (hadha) or هٰذِهِ (hadhihi)
Some: add ـِي (-i) to say my, as in حَقِيبَتِي (haqibati)
lessons.crossCurricular: English: 'my' is a possessive word, like كِتَابِي (kitabi) my book
lessons.smsc: Moral: looking after my own things and other people's things

keywords.def: the round ta at the end of most girl words

hook.text: In Arabic, a bag is a girl word and a book is a boy word. How do you think we can tell?
hook.a: Most girl words end in ة (ta marbutah).

islamicLink.text: Arabic is the language of the Qur'an (Yusuf 12:2). In the Qur'an, words change for boys and girls too, so learning this now helps us read it well.

starter.q: Bismillah. What does هٰذَا (hadha) mean? A) this B) that C) my
Say: My name is ... in Arabic.
Which is far: هٰذَا or ذٰلِكَ?

teach.heading: Boy words and girl words
teach.note: Read each card. Pupils show 1 or 2 fingers. Circle the ة on each girl word.

teach.heading: This for girl words
bullets: هٰذَا كِتَابٌ (hadha kitabun) this is a book
هٰذِهِ حَقِيبَةٌ (hadhihi haqibatun) this is a bag
teach.note: Hold up a book, then a bag. Pupils say the right sentence.

teach.heading: Saying my
teach.note: Show that -i means my. Pupils hold up their own pen: qalami.

teach.heading: My with girl words
teach.note: Write the change slowly. The round ta opens out to an ordinary ta before -i.

misconception.right: حَقِيبَتِي (haqibati): ة becomes ت before ـِي

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.why: حَقِيبَتِي: the ة of حَقِيبَةٌ becomes ت and ـِي (my) is added.

practice.model:
Look at the end: ة, so it is a girl word.
Girl word, so use هٰذِهِ.
Say: hadhihi sayyaratun.

independent.q: Core: Copy and finish with هٰذَا or هٰذِهِ: ___ بَابٌ / ___ مَدْرَسَةٌ / ___ قَلَمٌ / ___ سَيَّارَةٌ
independent.a: هٰذَا بَابٌ / هٰذِهِ مَدْرَسَةٌ / هٰذَا قَلَمٌ / هٰذِهِ سَيَّارَةٌ
independent.model: Teacher does the first: بَابٌ has no ة, so هٰذَا بَابٌ.

independent.q: Extend: Write 'my' for: كِتَابٌ، حَقِيبَةٌ، مَدْرَسَةٌ
Stretch: Write one sentence: هٰذِهِ ... with 'my', e.g. this is my bag.

exit.q: Which word is a girl word? A) قَلَمٌ B) مَدْرَسَةٌ C) بَابٌ
Big question: how can I tell if an Arabic word is a girl word?
exit.a: It usually ends in ة (ta marbutah).

lessons.homework: Find three things at home, say هٰذَا or هٰذِهِ for each, then say 'my' for one of them.
lessons.send: SEND: blue and pink cards for boy and girl words. EAL: picture beside each word. Stretch: try 'your' to a boy: كِتَابُكَ (kitabuka).

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Special days, summer and numbers
lessons.title: Special days: Friday and the two Eids
lessons.bigQuestion: Which days are special for Muslims, and how do we name them in Arabic?
objectives: To understand how to name Friday and the two Eids in Arabic
successCriteria: All: say يَوْمُ الجُمُعَةِ (yawm al-jumu'ah)
Most: name عِيدُ الفِطْرِ and عِيدُ الأَضْحَى
Some: say a sentence: اليَوْمُ يَوْمُ الجُمُعَةِ (al-yawm yawm al-jumu'ah)
lessons.crossCurricular: Islamic Studies: Friday prayer and the two Eids
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: Friday and the Eids as gifts from Allah to the Muslims

keywords.def: Friday, the day of Jumu'ah prayer
the Eid of the sacrifice, at Hajj time

hook.text: What makes a day special? Which day of the week is special for Muslims?
hook.a: Friday, the day of Jumu'ah. Also the two Eids each year.

islamicLink.text: Allah tells the believers that when the call to prayer is made on Friday, they should hurry to remember Allah (al-Jumu'ah 62:9). The surah is even named after Friday: al-Jumu'ah.

starter.q: Bismillah. Is مَدْرَسَةٌ a boy word or a girl word? A) boy B) girl

teach.heading: Friday
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Say each word, pupils echo three times. Ask who goes to the masjid on Friday with family.

teach.heading: The two Eids
teach.note: Muslims have two Eids each year. Ramadan begins soon after this half term, so 'id al-fitr is coming.

teach.heading: A sentence
teach.note: Build it word by word: al-yawm (today), yawm al-jumu'ah (Friday). Pupils say it as a chant (spoken, no tune).

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.why: 'Id al-fitr is the Eid of breaking the fast, after Ramadan. 'Id al-adha is at Hajj time.

practice.model:
Start with يَوْمُ (yawm), day.
Add الجُمُعَةِ (al-jumu'ah).
Say it together: yawm al-jumu'ah.

practice.q: What do we say to someone on Eid?
Which Eid is at Hajj time?

independent.q: Core: Copy and match: يَوْمُ الجُمُعَةِ / عِيدُ الفِطْرِ / عِيدُ الأَضْحَى with Friday / Eid after Ramadan / Eid at Hajj time.
independent.a: يَوْمُ الجُمُعَةِ = Friday; عِيدُ الفِطْرِ = Eid after Ramadan; عِيدُ الأَضْحَى = Eid at Hajj time
independent.model: Teacher matches the first: يَوْمُ الجُمُعَةِ has يَوْمُ, day, so it is Friday.

independent.q: Extend: Make an Eid card (shapes and patterns, no people) and write عِيدٌ مُبَارَكٌ on it.
independent.a: Card with عِيدٌ مُبَارَكٌ written neatly

independent.q: Stretch: Write: اليَوْمُ يَوْمُ الجُمُعَةِ and say what it means.

exit.q: What is Friday in Arabic? A) يَوْمُ الجُمُعَةِ B) عِيدُ الفِطْرِ C) مَسْجِد
Big question: which days are special for Muslims, and what are they called in Arabic?
exit.a: Friday يَوْمُ الجُمُعَةِ, and the two Eids: عِيدُ الفِطْرِ and عِيدُ الأَضْحَى.

lessons.homework: On Friday, say اليَوْمُ يَوْمُ الجُمُعَةِ to someone at home and tell them what it means.
lessons.send: SEND: three picture cards (masjid, dates, Ka'bah photo) to match. EAL: word mat with Arabic, sound and English. Stretch: say 'I go to the masjid': أَذْهَبُ إِلَى المَسْجِدِ (adhhabu ila l-masjid).

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Special days, summer and numbers
lessons.title: Summer: the weather and what we do
lessons.bigQuestion: How can I talk about summer weather in Arabic?
objectives: To understand how to describe summer weather and say what I do in summer
successCriteria: All: say الصَّيْفُ (as-sayf) and شَمْسٌ (shams)
Most: say الجَوُّ حَارٌّ (al-jawwu harrun)
Some: say what I do: فِي الصَّيْفِ أَسْبَحُ (fi s-sayf asbahu)
lessons.crossCurricular: Geography: hot and cold places and the seasons
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: thanking Allah for the sun and the changing seasons

hook.text: It is cold January now. What will be different in summer? Think of the sun, the sky and what you do.
hook.a: Hot, sunny, long days; we swim, play outside and drink lots of water.

islamicLink.text: Allah made the sun and the moon run to a fixed measure (ar-Rahman 55:5). The sun brings us summer, light and warmth by His command.

starter.q: Bismillah. What is Friday in Arabic? A) يَوْمُ الجُمُعَةِ B) عِيدُ الأَضْحَى
What do we say on Eid?
Winter word from Autumn: الشِّتَاءُ means ...?

teach.heading: Summer words
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Show the sun photo. Pupils echo each word, then point to the sun and say shams.

teach.heading: What is the weather?
teach.note: al-jaww is the weather. Pupils fan themselves for harr and shiver for barid as they say it.

teach.heading: What I do in summer
bullets: أَسْبَحُ (asbahu) I swim; أَلْعَبُ (al'abu) I play
أَشْرَبُ مَاءً (ashrabu ma'an) I drink water
teach.note: Act each verb. All three start with أَ, which means I.

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.why: حَارٌّ (harr) is hot; بَارِدٌ (barid) is cold.

practice.model:
Start with when: فِي الصَّيْفِ.
Then what I do: أَلْعَبُ.
Together: fi s-sayf al'abu.

independent.q: Core: Draw a sun and a pool (no people) and label them شَمْسٌ and الصَّيْفُ. Write الجَوُّ حَارٌّ underneath.
independent.model: Teacher draws a quick sun, writes شَمْسٌ beside it, then writes الجَوُّ حَارٌّ under the picture.

independent.q: Extend: Write two things you do in summer, starting فِي الصَّيْفِ.
independent.a: For example: فِي الصَّيْفِ أَسْبَحُ. فِي الصَّيْفِ أَشْرَبُ مَاءً.

independent.q: Stretch: Write one sentence about winter: الجَوُّ بَارِدٌ فِي الشِّتَاءِ.
independent.a: The weather is cold in winter.

exit.q: What is 'summer' in Arabic? A) الشِّتَاءُ B) الصَّيْفُ C) شَمْسٌ
Big question: describe summer weather in Arabic.
exit.a: الجَوُّ حَارٌّ (the weather is hot); there is شَمْسٌ (sun).

lessons.homework: Look out of the window each day this week and say الجَوُّ حَارٌّ or الجَوُّ بَارِدٌ.
lessons.send: SEND: hot and cold picture cards with the words. EAL: actions for each verb. Stretch: add أَيْضًا (aydan, also): فِي الصَّيْفِ أَسْبَحُ وَأَلْعَبُ أَيْضًا.

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Special days, summer and numbers
lessons.title: Numbers 1 to 10, read and written; unit check
lessons.bigQuestion: How do Arabic numbers look and sound?
objectives: To understand how to read, say and write the numbers 1 to 10 in Arabic
successCriteria: All: count from وَاحِد (wahid) to عَشَرَة ('asharah)
Most: read the digits ١ to ١٠
Some: write a number sum in Arabic digits, e.g. ٣ + ٢ = ٥
lessons.crossCurricular: Maths: the digits we use in English came to Europe through Muslim mathematicians
lessons.smsc: Cultural: Arabic digits and the Muslim scholars who spread them

keywords.def: review, going over what we learnt

hook.text: Look at this: ٥. What number do you think it is? Why might it look like that?
hook.a: It is 5 (khamsah). Arabic digits look different, but we use them the same way.

islamicLink.text: Allah made the night and day signs so that we may know the number of years and the counting of time (al-Isra 17:12). Counting is part of how we plan our prayers, fasts and days.

starter.q: Bismillah. What is 'summer'? A) الصَّيْفُ B) الشِّتَاءُ
Name one of the two Eids.

teach.heading: Count 1 to 5
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Count on fingers, pupils echo. Then count backwards.

teach.heading: Count 6 to 10
teach.note: Point out that ١٠ is written ١ then ٠, just like 10. Numbers are written left to right even in Arabic.

teach.heading: Spot the digit

misconception.right: ٦ is six (sittah); ٧ is seven (sab'ah): ٧ looks like a V

teach.note: Many pupils mix ٦ and ٧, and ٢ and ٣. Show them side by side.

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.why: ٥ is five; ٤ is four and ٦ is six.

teach.heading: Unit check: our words
teach.note: Quick review before the check. Pupils say each word as you point.

practice.q: Read: ٣ + ٢ = ٥ and say it in Arabic.
practice.a: ثَلَاثَة + اِثْنَان = خَمْسَة (thalathah wa ithnan: khamsah)
practice.model:
Read each digit: ٣ thalathah, ٢ ithnan, ٥ khamsah.
Say: thalathah wa ithnan, khamsah.

independent.q: Core (unit check, portal response box or paper): 1) Write ١ to ١٠ in order. 2) Match: الصَّيْفُ / شَمْسٌ / يَوْمُ الجُمُعَةِ with summer / sun / Friday.
independent.a: 1) ١ ٢ ٣ ٤ ٥ ٦ ٧ ٨ ٩ ١٠ 2) الصَّيْفُ summer; شَمْسٌ sun; يَوْمُ الجُمُعَةِ Friday
independent.model: Teacher writes ١ and ٢ first, saying wahid, ithnan, then matches الصَّيْفُ with summer.

independent.q: Extend: Write the sums in Arabic digits: 4 + 4 = 8; 6 + 3 = 9.
Stretch: Write الجَوُّ حَارٌّ and عِيدٌ مُبَارَكٌ and say when you would say each.
independent.a: On a hot day; on Eid.

exit.q: Which is ten? A) ١٠ B) ٧ C) ٦
Big question: how do Arabic numbers look and sound? Write ٥ and say it.

lessons.homework: Count ten things at home in Arabic, and find one place where you see Arabic digits (a clock, a book, a calendar).
lessons.send: SEND: number line ١ to ١٠ with the words. EAL: count real objects. Stretch: try 11 أَحَدَ عَشَرَ (ahada 'ashar).

hook.text: Which three things do you use every day to keep clean? Can you guess any of their Arabic names?

successCriteria: All: say أَغْسِلُ يَدَيَّ

hook.text: If you could say only one sentence in Arabic about keeping clean, what would it be?
hook.a: أَغْسِلُ يَدَيَّ (aghsilu yadayya): I wash my hands.

islamicLink.text: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Were it not that it would be hard on my ummah, I would have ordered them to use the siwak before every prayer' (Bukhari and Muslim).

teach.heading: I wash ...
bullets: أَغْسِلُ يَدَيَّ: I wash my hands
Act it as you say it
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. Mime washing; pupils copy. Spoken practice only; no songs or music.

teach.heading: Body words with 'my'
teach.note: Point to each part.

teach.heading: Brushing teeth
bullets: The Prophet ﷺ loved the siwak
teach.note: Siwak: Bukhari and Muslim report the Prophet ﷺ used it often.

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.why: وَجْهِي = my face.

practice.model: Teacher: start with أَغْسِلُ (I wash), then the body word with 'my': قَدَمَيَّ. Together: أَغْسِلُ قَدَمَيَّ.

independent.q: Write three wudu-order sentences on the pupil PDF: 1) أَغْسِلُ يَدَيَّ 2) أَغْسِلُ وَجْهِي 3) أَغْسِلُ قَدَمَيَّ, then read them aloud to the camera.
independent.a: Three sentences copied accurately and read aloud
independent.model: Teacher writes sentence 1 slowly, naming each letter and haraka.

independent.q: Extend: add 'with soap': أَغْسِلُ يَدَيَّ بِالصَّابُونِ.
independent.a: I wash my hands with soap.

independent.q: Stretch: write 'I clean my teeth'.

exit.q: 'I wash' is ...
Back to our ponder: your one sentence?
exit.a: أَغْسِلُ يَدَيَّ: I wash my hands.

lessons.homework: Each time you wash your hands this week, say أَغْسِلُ يَدَيَّ.

hook.text: Look around your room. Which shape can you see the most? Guess its name in Arabic!
hook.a: Often the rectangle: مُسْتَطِيل (a door, a book, a screen).

teach.heading: Four shapes
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. Draw each shape on the board.

teach.heading: Shape and colour
teach.note: Point out: دَائِرَة ends in ة, so the colour is the girl form (حَمْرَاء).

teach.heading: Shapes in Islamic art
bullets: Islamic patterns use circles and stars
teach.note: Show a geometric tile pattern (no living things).

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.why: مُثَلَّث has three sides (ثَلَاثَة = three).

practice.q: Hold up a square shape and say it with its colour.
practice.a: For example: مُرَبَّعٌ أَزْرَقُ (a blue square)
practice.model: Teacher holds a blue square: 'مُرَبَّعٌ أَزْرَقُ'. Shape first, then colour.

practice.q: How many sides has a مُثَلَّث?

independent.q: Colour and label the pattern on the pupil PDF: write the Arabic shape name in each shape and count how many of each.
independent.a: Shapes labelled correctly; counts written as Arabic numbers
independent.model: Teacher labels one circle دَائِرَة and writes the count of circles as an Arabic numeral, for example ٣.

independent.q: Extend: say 'a yellow triangle'.
Stretch: why is the colour حَمْرَاء with دَائِرَة?
independent.a: دَائِرَة is a girl word (ends in ة), so the colour is the girl form.

exit.q: Rectangle is ...
Back to our ponder: which shape is most in your room?

lessons.bigQuestion: In English, thirteen is 'three and ten'. How do you think Arabic says 13?
objectives: To understand how to say, read and write the Arabic numbers from 1 to 20

lessons.crossCurricular: Maths: number and place value to 20

hook.text: In English, thirteen is 'three and ten'. How do you think Arabic says 13?
hook.a: The same idea: ثَلَاثَةَ عَشَرَ (thalathata 'ashar): three-ten.

teach.heading: 1 to 10 again
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. Count together with fingers. Spoken practice only; no songs or music.

teach.heading: 11 to 20
teach.note: Pattern: number + عَشَرَ.

teach.heading: Number line
teach.note: Point and count.

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.why: ١٧ = seventeen: سَبْعَةَ عَشَرَ.

practice.q: Say 14 and write it in Arabic numerals.
practice.model: Teacher: 14 = four and ten: أَرْبَعَة + عَشَرَ = أَرْبَعَةَ عَشَرَ. Written ١٤: the 1 (١) then the 4 (٤), left to right like English.

independent.q: Number match on the pupil PDF: join ١١ to ٢٠ to their Arabic words, then write the answers to five sums in Arabic numerals (e.g. ١٠ + ٥).
independent.model: Teacher does ١٠ + ٥ = ١٥ (خَمْسَةَ عَشَرَ).

independent.q: Extend: count backwards from 20 to 11.
Stretch: how many prayers in a day plus how many rak'ahs in Fajr? Say it in Arabic.

exit.q: Back to our ponder: how does Arabic say 13?

lessons.homework: Count 20 things at home (spoons, steps) out loud in Arabic.
lessons.send: SEND: number line with words. EAL: number cards. Stretch: write all numbers 11 to 20 from memory.

lessons.title: My book, your book: attached pronouns
lessons.bigQuestion: In Arabic, one tiny ending can turn 'book' into 'my book'. Why might that be useful?
objectives: To understand how small endings on a word show whose it is (my, your, his, her)
successCriteria: All: say كِتَابِي (my book)
Most: change a word with -ي، -كَ، -هُ، -هَا
Some: use the endings with three different nouns

hook.text: In Arabic, one tiny ending can turn 'book' into 'my book'. Why might that be useful?
hook.a: It is short and quick: كِتَاب becomes كِتَابِي with just one letter.

teach.heading: Endings that show whose
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah.

teach.heading: Words ending in ة
bullets: ة becomes ت before the ending
teach.note: Show the round ة opening into ت.

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.why: ـهَا = her.

practice.model: Teacher: قَلَم + ـِي = قَلَمِي. Point to your own pen as you say it.

independent.q: Ending grid on the pupil PDF: add -ي، -كَ، -هُ، -هَا to قَلَم، كِتَاب and بَيْت, then read three aloud.
independent.a: قَلَمِي، قَلَمُكَ، قَلَمُهُ، قَلَمُهَا; كِتَابِي ...; بَيْتِي، بَيْتُكَ، بَيْتُهُ، بَيْتُهَا
independent.model: Teacher fills the قَلَم row on screen.

independent.q: Extend: say 'my towel' and 'my bag'.
Stretch: hold up an object and say 'this is my ...'.

exit.q: كِتَابِي means ...
Back to our ponder: why is a tiny ending useful?
exit.a: It shows whose something is in one letter or two.

lessons.homework: Label five of your things at home with 'my ...' in Arabic on sticky notes.
lessons.send: SEND: ending cards to stick on words. EAL: colour-coded endings. Stretch: use -كِ for a girl and -كَ for a boy correctly.

lessons.title: My grandfather, grandmother and relatives
lessons.bigQuestion: English has one word for 'uncle'. Arabic has two. Why might it help to know whose side of the family someone is on?
objectives: To understand and use Arabic words for grandparents and relatives in short sentences
successCriteria: All: say four family words: جَدّ، جَدَّة، عَمّ، خَال
Most: introduce a relative with هٰذَا or هٰذِهِ
Some: explain the difference between عَمّ and خَال

hook.text: English has one word for 'uncle'. Arabic has two. Why might it help to know whose side of the family someone is on?
hook.a: Arabic shows the family link: عَمّ is your father's brother, خَال is your mother's brother.

islamicLink.text: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Whoever would like his provision to be increased and his life to be extended, let him keep the ties of kinship' (Bukhari and Muslim).

teach.heading: My grandparents
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. Pupils repeat three times. Spoken practice only; no songs or music.

teach.heading: Two kinds of uncle and aunt
teach.note: Point to each side of the family tree.

teach.heading: Introducing a relative
bullets: هٰذَا جَدِّي (hadha jaddi): this is my grandfather
هٰذِهِ جَدَّتِي (hadhihi jaddati): this is my grandmother
هٰذَا for boys and men, هٰذِهِ for girls and women
teach.note: Recall هٰذَا / هٰذِهِ from the bridge lessons.

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.why: خَال (khal) is the mother's brother.

practice.model: Teacher: grandmother is a woman, so هٰذِهِ; then جَدَّة + ـِي = جَدَّتِي. Together: هٰذِهِ جَدَّتِي.

independent.q: Make a family tree on the pupil PDF with names only (no drawings of people): label each box with the Arabic word and write two sentences with هٰذَا or هٰذِهِ.
independent.a: Correct labels (جَدّ، جَدَّة، عَمّ، عَمَّة، خَال، خَالَة) and two correct sentences
independent.model: Teacher labels the father's brother box عَمّ and writes: هٰذَا عَمِّي.

independent.q: Extend: write 'this is my aunt' for your mother's sister.
Stretch: say how many uncles you have: عِنْدِي ... أَعْمَام.
independent.a: For example: عِنْدِي عَمَّانِ (I have two uncles)

exit.q: عَمَّة is ...
Back to our ponder: why two words for uncle?
exit.a: To show which side of the family

lessons.homework: Teach your family the Arabic words for your relatives and call one relative to say salam this week.
lessons.send: SEND: family tree with words to cut and stick. EAL: word mat with English. Stretch: use the plural أَعْمَام (uncles).

lessons.bigQuestion: If you went to a market in an Arabic-speaking country, which three words would you need most?
objectives: To understand how to say where I go and what I buy at the market in Arabic
successCriteria: All: say أَذْهَبُ إِلَى السُّوقِ
Most: say what I buy with أَشْتَرِي and a food word
Some: make a two-sentence market story
lessons.crossCurricular: Maths: counting items on a list
lessons.smsc: Social: polite shopping; Cultural: markets in Arabic-speaking countries

hook.text: If you went to a market in an Arabic-speaking country, which three words would you need most?
hook.a: Words like أَشْتَرِي (I buy), the food you want, and بِكَمْ؟ (how much?).

teach.heading: Going to the market
bullets: أَذْهَبُ إِلَى السُّوقِ: I go to the market
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. Walk on the spot as you say it. Spoken practice only; no songs or music.

teach.heading: At the market
teach.note: Hold up real food; pupils say the word.

teach.heading: I buy ...
bullets: أَشْتَرِي خُبْزًا (ashtari khubzan): I buy bread
أَشْتَرِي تُفَّاحًا (ashtari tuffahan): I buy apples
The ending ـًا shows the thing bought
teach.note: Keep the grammar light: notice the ending, no need to name it.

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.why: أَشْتَرِي = I buy; مَوْز = bananas.

practice.q: Say: I go to the market.
practice.model: Teacher builds it: أَذْهَبُ (I go) + إِلَى (to) + السُّوقِ (the market). Pupils repeat each part, then the whole.

independent.q: Write a shopping list on the pupil PDF: five foods in Arabic, then two sentences: أَذْهَبُ إِلَى السُّوقِ. أَشْتَرِي ... Read them to your partner.
independent.a: Five food words and two correct sentences
independent.model: Teacher writes: أَذْهَبُ إِلَى السُّوقِ. أَشْتَرِي خُبْزًا وَحَلِيبًا.

independent.q: Extend: add who you go with: مَعَ أَبِي (with my father).
Stretch: add your grandfather: مَعَ جَدِّي.

exit.q: سُوق is ...
Back to our ponder: which three words would you need?

lessons.homework: Next time you go shopping, say the Arabic name of three things you buy.

lessons.title: Verbs in the past tense: ذَهَبْتُ، أَكَلْتُ
lessons.bigQuestion: How do we show something already happened in English? Guess how Arabic might do it.
objectives: To understand how to say what I did in the past with verbs ending in ـتُ
successCriteria: All: say three past-tense verbs with 'I'
Most: change a present verb to the past
Some: write two sentences about what I did yesterday
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: reflecting on what we did

hook.text: How do we show something already happened in English? Guess how Arabic might do it.
hook.a: English often adds -ed; Arabic changes the verb and, for 'I', ends it with ـتُ.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it' (az-Zalzalah 99:7): all we did yesterday is written.

starter.q: Say: I go to the market.

teach.heading: Now and before
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. Read across each row.

teach.heading: The ـتُ ending
bullets: Past tense with 'I' ends in ـتُ
Listen for the tu at the end
teach.note: Pupils tap the table when they hear ـتُ. Spoken practice only; no songs or music.

teach.heading: Yesterday
bullets: Yesterday I went to the masjid
أَمْسِ أَكَلْتُ تَمْرًا: yesterday I ate dates
teach.note: Model the sentences with actions.

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.why: Past tense with 'I' ends in ـتُ.

practice.model: Teacher: أَلْعَبُ is 'I play' now. For the past, take لَعِبَ (he played) and add ـتُ: لَعِبْتُ, 'I played'.

independent.q: On the pupil PDF, match four present verbs to their past forms, then write two sentences starting with أَمْسِ about what you did yesterday.
independent.a: Matches: أَذْهَبُ ذَهَبْتُ، آكُلُ أَكَلْتُ، أَشْرَبُ شَرِبْتُ، أَلْعَبُ لَعِبْتُ; two correct sentences
independent.model: Teacher writes: أَمْسِ شَرِبْتُ حَلِيبًا (yesterday I drank milk).

independent.q: Extend: write 'I read' in the past: قَرَأْتُ.
Stretch: tell your partner three things you did at Eid in the past tense.
independent.a: For example: ذَهَبْتُ إِلَى المَسْجِدِ، أَكَلْتُ، لَعِبْتُ

exit.q: Past tense with 'I' ends in ...
Back to our ponder: how does Arabic show the past?
exit.a: It changes the verb; with 'I' it ends in ـتُ

lessons.homework: At dinner, tell your family two things you did today using ذَهَبْتُ, أَكَلْتُ or لَعِبْتُ.
lessons.send: SEND: verb cards with pictures to match. EAL: word mat with both forms. Stretch: say 'he went' (ذَهَبَ) and 'I went' (ذَهَبْتُ).

lessons.unit: Summer 1: My grandparents and relatives; the market; Ramadan and Eid
lessons.title: Pronouns and attached pronouns; reading a short passage
lessons.bigQuestion: When you read a story in a new language, what helps you understand it?
objectives: To understand pronouns and 'my, your, his, her' endings by reading a short passage aloud
successCriteria: All: say أَنَا، أَنْتَ، هُوَ، هِيَ
Most: read the passage aloud with the harakat
Some: answer questions on the passage in Arabic

hook.text: When you read a story in a new language, what helps you understand it?
hook.a: Known words, pictures, reading slowly and asking 'who? what?': we will use all of these.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'Read in the name of your Lord who created' (al-'Alaq 96:1).

teach.heading: Pronouns
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. Point to yourself, the camera, a boy word, a girl word.

teach.heading: My, your, his, her
bullets: كِتَابُهُ: his book; كِتَابُهَا: her book
teach.note: Recall Spring 2 lesson 12.

teach.heading: Our short passage
teach.note: Teacher reads, then pupils read line by line.

quote.text:
ذَهَبْتُ إِلَى السُّوقِ مَعَ جَدِّي.
اِشْتَرَى جَدِّي تَمْرًا.
أَكَلْتُ تَمْرَةً.
قَالَ جَدِّي: الحَمْدُ لِلّٰهِ.
quote.source: Our own short text (Kitabi passage to be checked)

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.q: In the passage, who bought the dates?
check.why: اِشْتَرَى جَدِّي تَمْرًا: my grandfather bought dates.

practice.q: Read line 1 aloud and say what it means.
practice.a: I went to the market with my grandfather.
practice.model: Teacher reads ذَهَبْتُ (I went) إِلَى السُّوقِ (to the market) مَعَ جَدِّي (with my grandfather), pointing to each word.

independent.q: On the pupil PDF: read the passage aloud to your partner, then answer in Arabic: مَعَ مَنْ ذَهَبْتُ؟ مَاذَا اِشْتَرَى جَدِّي؟ مَاذَا أَكَلْتُ؟
independent.model: Teacher answers question 1: مَعَ مَنْ ذَهَبْتُ؟ مَعَ جَدِّي.

independent.q: Extend: change جَدِّي to جَدَّتِي in line 1 and read it.
Stretch: write one more line for the passage.

exit.q: أَنَا means ...
Back to our ponder: what helped you read the passage?
exit.a: Known words, reading slowly, asking who and what

lessons.homework: Read the passage to a family member and teach them what الحَمْدُ لِلّٰهِ means.
lessons.send: SEND: passage with picture clues and the English under each line. EAL: pronoun cards. Stretch: rewrite the passage with هُوَ instead of أَنَا (ذَهَبَ، أَكَلَ).

lessons.unit: Summer 2: Clothes, autumn and spring; revision
lessons.title: Clothes: أَلْبَسُ (I wear)
lessons.bigQuestion: Why do you think Muslims wear their best clean clothes on Friday and Eid?
objectives: To understand and use Arabic words for clothes in short sentences with أَلْبَسُ and a colour
successCriteria: All: say five clothes words
Most: say what I wear with أَلْبَسُ
Some: add a colour that agrees: قَمِيصٌ أَبْيَضُ, قُبَّعَةٌ بَيْضَاءُ

hook.text: Why do you think Muslims wear their best clean clothes on Friday and Eid?
hook.a: To look our best for Allah and for prayer; Allah tells us to take our adornment to every masjid (7:31).

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'O children of Adam, take your adornment at every masjid' (al-A'raf 7:31).

starter.q: Say 'I go to the market' in Arabic.

teach.heading: Five clothes
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. Hold up real clothes on camera; pupils repeat three times. Spoken practice only; no songs or music.

teach.heading: I wear: أَلْبَسُ
bullets: After أَلْبَسُ the word ends in -an: قَمِيصًا
teach.note: Point to the two fathahs at the end: قَمِيصًا.

teach.heading: Boy words and girl words
bullets: Girl words end in ة, and the colour changes

check.why: قُبَّعَة is a girl word, so the colour is بَيْضَاءُ.

practice.model: Teacher: start with أَلْبَسُ (I wear). Then ثَوْب with the -an ending: ثَوْبًا. Together: أَلْبَسُ ثَوْبًا.

independent.q: On the pupil PDF, label five photos of clothes in Arabic, then write three sentences with أَلْبَسُ about what you wear on Friday.
independent.a: Five labels and sentences such as أَلْبَسُ ثَوْبًا. أَلْبَسُ قُبَّعَةً.
independent.model: Teacher labels the shirt قَمِيصٌ and writes أَلْبَسُ قَمِيصًا.

independent.q: Extend: add a colour to one sentence.
Stretch: say 'a white hat' and 'a white shirt'.

exit.q: قُبَّعَةٌ means ...
Back to our ponder: why wear our best clothes on Friday?
exit.a: To look our best for prayer (7:31)

lessons.homework: Lay out your Friday clothes and say each one in Arabic to your family.
lessons.send: SEND: picture flashcards with Arabic. EAL: word mat with English. Stretch: learn مِعْطَفٌ (coat) and جَوَارِبُ (socks).

lessons.unit: Summer 2: Clothes, autumn and spring; revision
lessons.title: Autumn and spring: الخَرِيفُ وَالرَّبِيعُ
lessons.bigQuestion: Why does Allah make the seasons change instead of keeping the same weather all year?
objectives: To understand and use the names of the four seasons and say what happens in autumn and spring
successCriteria: All: name the four seasons in Arabic
Most: say one sentence about autumn and one about spring
Some: describe the weather in each season with الجَوُّ
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: wonder at the changing seasons

hook.text: Why does Allah make the seasons change instead of keeping the same weather all year?
hook.a: So plants can grow, rest and grow again; the change is a sign of Allah's power (3:190).

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the night and the day are signs for those of understanding' (Al 'Imran 3:190).

teach.heading: Four seasons
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. Show a photo for each season. Spoken practice only; no songs or music.

teach.heading: Autumn: الخَرِيفُ
bullets: الجَوُّ بَارِدٌ قَلِيلًا: a little cold

check.why: الرَّبِيعُ is spring; الأَزْهَارُ are flowers.

teach.heading: The weather
teach.note: Recall الصَّيْف from Spring 1.

practice.q: Say: in autumn the leaves fall.
practice.model: Teacher: فِي (in), الخَرِيفِ (autumn, with kasrah after فِي), تَسْقُطُ (fall), الأَوْرَاقُ (the leaves).

independent.q: Seasons wheel on the pupil PDF: write the four seasons in Arabic around the circle and one weather sentence for each with الجَوُّ.
independent.a: الرَّبِيعُ: الجَوُّ مُعْتَدِلٌ؛ الصَّيْفُ: الجَوُّ حَارٌّ؛ الخَرِيفُ: الجَوُّ بَارِدٌ قَلِيلًا؛ الشِّتَاءُ: الجَوُّ بَارِدٌ
independent.model: Teacher fills summer: الصَّيْفُ: الجَوُّ حَارٌّ.

independent.q: Extend: write which season you like: أُحِبُّ ...

exit.q: الخَرِيفُ means ...
Back to our ponder: why do seasons change?
exit.a: So things grow and rest; a sign of Allah

lessons.homework: Look out of the window each day this week and tell your family the weather in Arabic.
lessons.send: SEND: season picture cards. EAL: word mat. Stretch: say 'in winter I wear a coat': فِي الشِّتَاءِ أَلْبَسُ مِعْطَفًا.

lessons.unit: Summer 2: Clothes, autumn and spring; revision
lessons.title: Revision of all Year 3 topics: مُرَاجَعَةٌ
lessons.bigQuestion: Which Arabic word from this year do you think you will never forget, and why?
objectives: To understand which Year 3 Arabic words and sentences I know well and practise the ones I find hard
successCriteria: All: answer quick questions from each half term
Most: read and translate four short sentences
Some: write two sentences of my own using words from different topics
lessons.smsc: Moral: effort and perseverance in learning

hook.text: Which Arabic word from this year do you think you will never forget, and why?
hook.a: Answers vary: a word we used every day, like صَابُونٌ or جَدِّي.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'And say: My Lord, increase me in knowledge' (Ta-Ha 20:114).

teach.heading: Our year in Arabic
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. Pupils call out a word for each.

timeline.label: Summer 1
timeline.text: Relatives, the market, Ramadan and Eid

teach.heading: Word sort
teach.note: Pupils sort the cards by topic.

check.why: ذَهَبْتُ = I went; السُّوق = the market.

practice.model: Teacher: أَغْسِلُ (I wash) and يَدَيَّ (my two hands). Together: I wash my hands.

practice.a: أَحَدَ عَشَرَ، اِثْنَا عَشَرَ، ثَلَاثَةَ عَشَرَ، أَرْبَعَةَ عَشَرَ، خَمْسَةَ عَشَرَ

independent.q: Revision circuit on the pupil PDF: four short tasks (match words to pictures; numbers 1 to 20; read and translate four sentences; write two sentences of your own).
independent.a: Correct matches, numbers and translations; two correct sentences
independent.model: Teacher does one match and one translation: قُبَّعَةٌ to the hat photo; هٰذَا جَدِّي = this is my grandfather.

independent.q: Write the three words you find hardest and practise them five times.

exit.q: سُؤَالٌ means ...
Back to our ponder: which word will you never forget?

lessons.homework: Practise your three hardest words with a family member before the assessment.
lessons.send: SEND: circuit tasks with picture support. EAL: bilingual word list. Stretch: write three sentences joining two topics.

lessons.unit: Summer 2: Clothes, autumn and spring; revision
lessons.title: End-of-year assessment: reading, writing and speaking
lessons.bigQuestion: What makes you feel calm before a test, and what helps you do your best?
objectives: To understand how much Arabic I can read, write and say by showing it in the end-of-year assessment
successCriteria: All: read five words and say two sentences
Most: read four sentences and write three words correctly
Some: write two full sentences and answer a question in Arabic

hook.text: What makes you feel calm before a test, and what helps you do your best?
hook.a: Bismillah, a du'a, a deep breath, and reading each question carefully.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'Read in the name of your Lord who created' (al-'Alaq 96:1).

teach.heading: Three parts
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. Speaking is one to one while others do reading and writing.

head: Part
What you do
Time
rows: Read words and sentences; match to pictures
Copy and write words and two sentences
Answer three questions with the teacher

teach.heading: Speaking questions
bullets: أَيُّ فَصْلٍ تُحِبُّ؟ (Which season do you like?)
teach.note: Model one answer: اِسْمِي ...؛ أَلْبَسُ ثَوْبًا؛ أُحِبُّ الرَّبِيعَ.

check.why: فَصْل = season; تُحِبُّ = you like.

practice.model: Teacher: the question has تَلْبَسُ (you wear), so I answer with أَلْبَسُ (I wear) and a clothes word: أَلْبَسُ ثَوْبًا.

independent.q: Reading part (pupil PDF assessment): match ten words to pictures and read four sentences.
independent.model: Teacher shows question 1: match قُبَّعَةٌ to the hat.

independent.q: Writing part: copy five words neatly and write two sentences (for example about clothes and seasons).
independent.a: Neat words with dots and harakat; two correct sentences

independent.q: Speaking part (while others write): three questions one to one with the teacher; recorded as secure, developing or not yet.
independent.a: Answers such as اِسْمِي ...؛ أَلْبَسُ ثَوْبًا؛ أُحِبُّ الرَّبِيعَ

exit.q: How did you find the assessment?
Back to our ponder: what helped you do your best?

lessons.homework: Read one Arabic page from your Kitabi book to your family over the summer each week.
lessons.send: SEND: reading part read with the teacher; picture answers allowed. EAL: instructions in English. Stretch: write three sentences and ask the teacher a question in Arabic.
